postTemplates.title: Moving from Experimentation to Production
postTemplates.text:
Feels like every week another company decides they need “something with AI” 😄

The difference now is that businesses are finally moving from experimentation into actual implementation — integrations, workflows, copilots, automation, internal tools, analytics, and AI-powered platforms.

Because of that, we’re currently speaking with companies looking for people with experience in:
• AI / LLM development
• Python & backend engineering
• AI agents and automation
• data pipelines & analytics
• cloud infrastructure for AI workloads
• product engineering around GenAI

If this sounds close to your background, send me your CV or message me directly. Happy to connect.

Also curious — what AI stack are you personally enjoying working with most right now?

postTemplates.text:
AI is moving insanely fast right now, and we’re seeing more and more companies looking for engineers and specialists who can actually build practical AI solutions — not just talk about them.

Right now we’re involved in several AI-related projects and discussions around:
• AI integrations
• LLM-based products

• intelligent workflows and tooling

– AI Engineers

postTemplates.title: Beyond the ChatGPT Gimmick: Hard Engineering
postTemplates.text:
It feels like we’ve finally moved past the "let’s just plug ChatGPT into it" phase. Companies aren’t just looking for AI gimmicks anymore they want actual utility.

The focus has shifted entirely to hard engineering: building reliable agentic workflows, setting up proper data pipelines, and making sure the infra can actually handle production loads without breaking the bank.

Because we're knee-deep in this shift right now, we’re looking to connect with engineers who have hands-on experience in:
* Heavy Python & backend architecture
* Building and steering AI agents
* LLM integration and fine-tuning
* Scalable data pipelines
* Cloud infra tailored for heavy AI workloads

If you’re currently building in this space and want to chat about what's next, drop your CV or just send a message. Always down to connect.

For anyone already in the trenches: what’s the biggest bottleneck you’re running into while trying to take an AI feature from prototype to production?

postTemplates.title: The AI Gold Rush Is Ending: Focus on Utility
postTemplates.text:
The AI gold rush phase seems to be ending.

Not because AI is slowing down. Because companies are getting more practical.

A year ago, everyone wanted an AI chatbot.
Today, they're asking tougher questions:
• Can it integrate with our systems?
• Can it access the right data?
• Can we trust the outputs?
• Can we operate it at scale without burning money?

The conversation has shifted from experimentation to execution.

The teams creating the most value right now aren't necessarily building the newest models. They're building the infrastructure, workflows, and products around them.

We're actively connecting with engineers who have experience in:
• Python & backend systems
• AI agents and agent orchestration
• LLM integrations
• Data pipelines and retrieval systems
• Cloud infrastructure for AI workloads

If that's your world and you're open to new opportunities, send me your CV or drop me a message.

One thing I'm curious about: What's the biggest gap between how AI projects look in demos versus how they behave in production?
postTemplates.bestFor: LinkedIn AI, Enterprise AI, Technical Slack channels

postTemplates.title: Demo vs Production Reality
postTemplates.text:
Getting an AI demo working has never been easier.
Getting it into production has never been harder.

Most teams can build a proof of concept in days. Then reality arrives.
• Data quality.
• Permissions.
• Latency.
• Infrastructure costs.
• Monitoring.
• Evaluation.
• Security.

Suddenly the challenge isn't AI anymore. It's engineering.

That's why we're seeing growing demand for people who understand both modern software architecture and AI systems.

We're looking to connect with engineers experienced in:
• Backend-heavy Python development
• AI agents and automation workflows
• LLM implementation and optimization
• Data engineering
• Cloud-native AI infrastructure

If you're working in this space and would be interested in discussing opportunities, feel free to send your CV or reach out directly.

For those building AI products today: What's consuming more time on your projects—the model itself or everything around it?
postTemplates.bestFor: High engagement across Discord LangChain & LinkedIn AI Pivot

postTemplates.title: Behind the Scenes of Production AI Systems
postTemplates.text:
Everyone wants AI. Very few want the engineering work required to make AI useful.

The exciting part isn't generating a response anymore.
It's everything behind the scenes:
• Reliable workflows
• Data pipelines
• System integrations
• Infrastructure optimization
• Evaluation and monitoring

That's where projects succeed or fail.

We're spending a lot of time helping companies move beyond prototypes and into production-ready AI systems, and one thing is becoming clear: The market needs more engineers who can bridge AI and software engineering.

Particularly people with experience in:
• Python and backend architecture
• Agentic AI systems
• LLM integrations
• Data platforms
• Cloud infrastructure

If you have experience in this area and are open to hearing about interesting opportunities, send me your CV or drop me a message.

I'd also love to hear from others building in this space: What has been the most unexpected bottleneck in your AI journey so far?
